clue.text: Excited with container for drawers to cover furniture

parts.note: someone excited or worked up is said to be up
a holster holds the gun of a person who draws a weapon, a drawer

explanation.surface: An excited instruction about storing chests of drawers under covers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawers' looks like furniture, but here it means gunslingers who draw their pistols.
explanation.definitionFit: To upholster is to fit padding and fabric over chairs and sofas.

clue.text: Surprise result, winning place

parts.note: a side that is ahead in a game is said to be up
to set something is to place or put it down

explanation.surface: A shock outcome in a race where the favourite only came second or third.
explanation.definitionFit: In sport an upset is an unexpected victory by the outsider.

clue.text: Properly assembled furniture shouldn't appear unstable

definitions.meaning: literally, well-built furniture ought to have no fixing working free
figuratively, the idiom for seeming mentally unhinged

explanation.surface: Advice that flatpack furniture put together correctly ought not to wobble.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone slightly crazy, mentally unsound, as though a fixing had come adrift; literally it is what good furniture lacks.

clue.text: One observes fool hugging fair Queen

indicators.note: the word for a fool wraps its arms round the other pieces, holding them inside

parts.note: a loon is a silly or foolish person
fair, in the sense of passable, is OK
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the standard abbreviation for the Queen

explanation.surface: A spectator watches a simpleton embracing a handsome monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectator who watches without joining in is an onlooker, a bystander.

clue.text: Uprising revealed decay, with America involved

indicators.note: in a down entry rising means the words for revealed and decay are read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a secret that is revealed is out
rot is decay
US is the United States of America

explanation.surface: A rebellion exposed corruption, and the United States had a hand in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uprising' works because this is a down entry: the two words are read from the bottom up.
explanation.definitionFit: Something involved is complicated and convoluted, as a tortuous argument twists and turns.

clue.text: Portly about fatty's middle?

annotationWithheld.why: Portly about fatty's middle? (6): ROUND (about) around T (middle of fatty), but 'about' must give ROUND and also signal the containment, one word doing two jobs

clue.text: Those in circus seeing assistant's backflip on to magician's head

indicators.note: the head of the magician's name is its first letter
a backflip turns the word for an assistant over, so it is read backwards

parts.note: an aide is an assistant

explanation.surface: Circus spectators watch the magician's helper perform a backflip onto his head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circus' suggests a big top, but the definition is the media circus, the press pack.
explanation.definitionFit: A media circus is the frenzy of press coverage, so the journalists are those in it.

clue.text: Part that is in witty remark, with funny ending

indicators.note: the abbreviation for that is goes inside the word for a witty remark

parts.note: a mot (bon mot) is a witty saying
i.e. (id est) means that is

indicators.note: the ending of funny is its last letter

explanation.surface: A joke that is only partly clever, rescued by a comic punchline.
explanation.definitionFit: A moiety is a half or a portion, a share of something.

clue.text: In a war, ideal guy to restore captured vehicle to the road

indicators.note: the rearranged letters capture the vehicle, holding it inside
restoring rearranges the letters of a war, ideal guy into a fresh order

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: In wartime a hero repairs a seized truck and gets it back on the highway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is a link word, not fodder; a dual carriageway is the British name for a divided highway.
explanation.definitionFit: A dual carriageway is a British road with a central reservation dividing the two directions of traffic, like a divided highway.

clue.text: Where one might land a fee, ultimately, stick with capital

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of fee

parts.note: a rod is a stick
Rome is the capital of Italy

explanation.surface: Instructions to pay a fee, then a stick and some money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' suggests money, but it is the capital city Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerodrome is an airfield where an aircraft lands.

clue.text: Various extraordinary people worship Him

indicators.note: something extraordinary is out of the usual order, so the letters of various are rearranged

explanation.surface: Many unusual folk are devoted to the divine.
explanation.definitionFit: Christians worship Christ as the Redeemer who delivers them from sin.

clue.text: Very little to inspire in parting tresses on top of toupee

indicators.note: the top of the toupee is its first letter
the word in parts the hair, sitting between its letters

parts.note: tresses are hair

explanation.surface: A balding man with hardly any inspiration, putting a parting in the hair of his wig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inspire' means breathe in: there is almost nothing in the air to inhale.
explanation.definitionFit: Thin air is air with little oxygen, so very little to breathe in; inspire here means inhale.

clue.text: Outline suggestion

definitions.meaning: to copy the outline of a drawing by following its lines
a faint hint, as in a touch of irony

explanation.definitionFit: To trace is to draw an outline, and a trace of something is a slight suggestion of it.

clue.text: As The Invisible Man's wandering continued?

definitions.text: As The Invisible Man's wandering continued?

indicators.note: letters that wander move about, so continued is rearranged

explanation.surface: The Invisible Man kept on roaming, as nobody spotted him.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: the Invisible Man roams on without anyone seeing him.
explanation.definitionFit: The Invisible Man cannot be seen, so his progress goes unseen by everyone.

clue.text: Pretence in government department one might rumble as junior official

indicators.note: the word for pretence goes in the government department's abbreviation

parts.note: FO is the Foreign Office, a British government department
an act is a pretence, as in putting on an act
a tum, a tummy, is something that might rumble when hungry

explanation.surface: A minor civil servant in a ministry suspected of putting on a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rumble' suggests exposing a fraud, but here it is the noise of a hungry stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: A factotum is a general helper or dogsbody doing all kinds of minor jobs.

clue.text: Child left unfolding plaits

indicators.note: plaits twist and weave strands, so the letters of unfolding are interwoven anew

explanation.surface: A girl abandoned while her braids come undone.
explanation.definitionFit: A foundling is an infant abandoned by its parents and found by others.

clue.text: Musical direction taken in familiar concerti

indicators.note: the answer is taken in, held within, the words familiar concerti

explanation.surface: A note on a score found in well-known concertos.
explanation.definitionFit: Arco tells string players to use the bow again after pizzicato.

clue.text: Nameless rogue traders

indicators.note: rogue as in wild and out of control, so the letters of nameless go astray

explanation.surface: Dishonest dealers who refuse to give their names.
explanation.definitionFit: Salesmen are people who trade, selling goods for a living.

clue.text: Sweet items with treacly centre stuffed into pockets

indicators.note: the middle letters are stuffed into the word for pockets, going inside

parts.note: to pocket something is to take it, as a thief takes

indicators.note: the centre of treacly is its middle letters

explanation.surface: Sugary buns with gooey fillings shoved into somebody's pockets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pockets' looks like a noun, but it is a verb: steals. 'centre' takes the middle three letters of treacly, not just one.
explanation.definitionFit: Teacakes are sweet buns with dried fruit, served toasted and buttered.

clue.text: Drug addict leaves torchbearer disheartened

indicators.note: losing its heart means the middle letter of the torchbearer word is removed

parts.note: a cinema usher carries a torch to show people to their seats

explanation.surface: An addict quits his job with the Olympic torch, his spirit broken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'torchbearer' suggests the Olympics; an usher carries a torch, a British word for a flashlight, in a dark cinema.
explanation.definitionFit: A user, in slang, is someone who takes illegal drugs.

clue.text: Out beyond this, mean business

parts.note: base, like mean, can describe something low or contemptible
a line is a line of business, a trade

explanation.surface: A threat that unless you get out, they mean business.
explanation.walkthrough: In tennis a ball landing past the baseline is called out.
explanation.definitionFit: The baseline marks the back of a tennis court; a shot beyond it is out.

clue.text: Problem to sort out

definitions.meaning: to sieve, sifting earth or gravel to separate it

explanation.definitionFit: A riddle is a puzzling question, and to riddle soil is to sieve it, separating coarse from fine.

clue.text: Protection from the wet geek

definitions.meaning: a boring obsessive, named after the jackets worn by trainspotters

explanation.definitionFit: The waterproof hooded jacket gave its name to the obsessive hobbyist who traditionally wears one.

clue.text: Affair that's horrid's ending marriage

indicators.note: the ending of horrid is its last letter

parts.note: a marriage is an alliance between two families

explanation.surface: A love affair whose awful consequence was the end of a marriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ending' looks like a verb, finishing the marriage, but it picks the last letter of horrid.
explanation.definitionFit: A dalliance is a casual romantic or sexual affair.

clue.text: Smoke one's beginning to get between wheels

indicators.note: the other pieces go between the letters of the word for wheels

parts.note: wheels is slang for a car
one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: the beginning to get is its first letter

explanation.surface: Lighting up while behind the wheel of a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wheels' is slang for a car; I and G go inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A cigar is something one smokes.

clue.text: Something shining over material

parts.note: a ray is a beam of light shining out
on means over, as in a cover on a table

explanation.surface: A glossy fabric laid over something.
explanation.definitionFit: Rayon is a synthetic fabric made from cellulose.

clue.text: Are brothers so organised?

definitions.meaning: monks, called brothers, belong to a religious order

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means neatly arranged, and monks are literally members of a monastic order.

clue.text: Allow room for a garden in spring

indicators.note: the letter and garden go in the spring month, inside its letters

parts.note: May is a month of spring
Kew Gardens is the royal botanic garden in London

explanation.surface: Leave space for a garden to be planted in springtime.
explanation.definitionFit: To make way is to stand aside and leave space for someone.

clue.text: English composer's written about in flier

indicators.note: written about, turned round, means the letters are set down backwards

parts.note: Alban Berg was an Austrian composer

explanation.surface: An English composer features in an article in an aviation magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'written about' reverses E and BERG together, giving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The grebe is a diving waterbird, so it flies; a flier is anything that flies.

clue.text: Leader knowing a couple of names in Norfolk town

parts.note: a king is the leader of his people
knowing, as in a knowing look, means sly
N is the abbreviation for name, so two of them make NN

explanation.surface: A clued-up ruler visits a couple of named people in an East Anglian town.
explanation.walkthrough: Norfolk is a county in eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: King's Lynn is a market port town in the English county of Norfolk.
